14	`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
15	matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
16	marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:

22	  markers). Under pc mode the csrwi markers are inert on BOTH legs: the QEMU plugin
23	  bypasses the CSR matcher when `enter_pc` is set (`hybrid_handoff.c:69-72`) and
24	  vsim skips the ELF csrwi scan when `exit_pc` is set (`simulator.hpp:223-247`). So
25	  T2 stays on the MARKED build but triggers on REAL function names:
26	  `vmatmul_kernel` -> `scalar_matmul_verify` (both `noinline`, F1). It keeps

# Roadmap: run all 7 demos on one RVV GEMM workload

## Goal

Every demo under `tests/demos/` (T1..T7) should showcase its switching mechanism on
the SAME RVV-intrinsic GEMM, so the suite reads as "one workload, seven ways to
switch QEMU <-> vsim." Today demos split between `rt_c_v_regs` and `icount_spin`.

We reuse the existing GEMM `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` (16x16x16 outer-product,
`__riscv_vle32` / `__riscv_vmacc_vx` / `__riscv_vse32`).

## Why two builds of one source

`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:

- Marker-driven demos (csr, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
- Count/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.
- pc: no longer marker-bound (F0). pc mode resolves an ROI from `ROI_START` /
  `ROI_END` (symbol name or `0x` address; default to the `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc`
  markers). Under pc mode the csrwi markers are inert on BOTH legs: the QEMU plugin
  bypasses the CSR matcher when `enter_pc` is set (`hybrid_handoff.c:69-72`) and
  vsim skips the ELF csrwi scan when `exit_pc` is set (`simulator.hpp:223-247`). So
  T2 stays on the MARKED build but triggers on REAL function names:
  `vmatmul_kernel` -> `scalar_matmul_verify` (both `noinline`, F1). It keeps
  REPEAT=1 so the vsim leg runs ONE GEMM; the MARKERLESS twin (REPEAT=200) would
  make vsim execute 200 GEMMs - fine for count modes, far too slow for a pc oneshot.

Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.

### Confirmed findings (probed on the built artifacts)
- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.
  The kernel is inlined at `-O1`, so a PC-range assertion has no symbol to anchor on.
  Fix: mark `vmatmul_kernel` `noinline` (also keeps it in the ROI per
  `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:49-51`).

  `trigger_kind="csr"`. So T6 and T7 must use the MARKED build.

| Demo | Mode     | Build      | ELF                    |
|------|----------|------------|------------------------|
| T1   | csr      | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T2   | pc       | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T3   | icount   | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T4   | bbv      | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T5   | slice    | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T6   | archive  | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T7   | simpoint | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |

T7 keeps current behavior: its small slice/icount targets profile the crt0+init
prefix BEFORE the enter marker (same regime as today's `rt_c_v_regs`); the kernel
runs in the M7 vsim replay leg.

---

### F1 - GEMM source: marker macro + noinline kernel + repeat loop
- State: TODO

meta = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
assert meta.get("schema") == 1, f"schema {meta.get('schema')!r}"
assert meta.get("abi_version") == 1, f"abi_version {meta.get('abi_version')!r}"
assert meta.get("abi_magic", "").lower() in ("0x42594841", "42594841"), \

assert meta.get("mem_size") == 134217728, f"mem_size {meta.get('mem_size')!r}"

echo "[demo M6+M7 4/4] verify replay advanced PC past archive"
REPLAY_STATE=""

  if [ -s "$cand" ]; then

print(hex(struct.unpack('<Q', open('$SNAP_DIR/state.bin', 'rb').read()[16:24])[0]))")

aiTitle: Understand archive mode and markers in GEMM

content.text:
## Archive mode (T6)

A two-step **snapshot-and-replay** flow, split across two separate runs:

- **Step A (M6, emit):** QEMU runs the workload, drains its full architectural state at the enter marker, and writes a portable snapshot to disk: `snap/0/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}` (registers + 128MB memory image + metadata).
- **Step B (M7, replay):** A fresh process loads that snapshot into a new `/dev/shm` mmap and resumes execution on the chosen model (vsim by default).

The point: the snapshot is **portable across sessions/processes**. You capture once, replay any number of times later without re-running QEMU1. The other 6 modes do a live in-memory QEMU->vsim->QEMU round-trip; archive mode persists the handoff state to disk in between.

## Why markers are needed

Markers = the `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (enter) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) instructions planted in the workload. They tell the system **where** to switch between QEMU and vsim.

Archive mode specifically needs them because the orchestrator is **marker-driven** (gemm_modes.md:37-39):
- `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` passes the plugin only `outfile=...` (no count target).
- `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py` sets replay `trigger_kind="csr"`.

So the only thing that tells QEMU when to stop and drain is hitting the CSR marker. That is why T6 (and T7, simpoint) must use the **MARKED** build of the GEMM, while count/profile modes (icount/bbv/slice) use the marker-free build (gemm_modes.md:18-19).

The two trigger families:
- **Marker-based** (csr, archive, simpoint): switch *at a specific instruction* the workload announces.
- **Count/profile-based** (icount, bbv, slice): switch *after N instructions* - here a marker would fire early and abort before reaching the count target, so it must be absent.

(pc mode is the exception - it resolves the ROI from symbol names/addresses, so markers are inert there.)
